title: Singapore Energy Resilience Strategy: An Off-grid and Micro-grid Power Using Smart Energy Management Solutions to be Deployed Island-wide
what_it_is: Singapore Energy Resilience Strategy: An Off-grid and Micro-grid Power Using Smart Energy Management Solutions to be Deployed Island-wide

sections.label: Gas dependence and blackout risk
sections.summary: About 95% of electricity comes from imported natural gas, and supply interruptions or plant failures could cause a system-wide blackout.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Approximately 95% of our electricity is generated from natural gas, imported via pipelines from neighbouring countries and liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These gas-fired combined-cycle plants are highly efficient, but they remain single-point-of-failure risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A supply interruption from a foreign source, a gas pipeline breach or a simultaneous failure of two major plants could cascade into a system-wide blackout.

sections.label: Public housing backup lacking
sections.summary: Public housing estates, home to 80% of the population, largely lack backup beyond stairwell emergency lighting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Public housing estates, which house 80% of our population, largely lack any form of backup beyond emergency lighting in stairwells.

sections.label: HDB rooftop solar potential
sections.summary: A typical 1,500 square metre HDB roof can host 250 to 300 kilowatt-peak solar, generating about 340 megawatt-hour yearly for daylight needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore's solar irradiance of approximately 1,580 kilowatt/square metre/year, a typical HDB block roof of 1,500 square metres can host a 250 to 300 kilowatt-peak system, generating roughly 340 megawatt-hour annually – enough to cover common area and essential load needs during daylight hours.

sections.label: MacPherson constituency microgrid example
sections.summary: The MacPherson microgrid has 80 HDB blocks with 12 megawatt-hour batteries, 20 shophouses and five industrial buildings with one megawatt-hour each.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I will give you an example of the MacPherson constituency microgrid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are 80 HDB blocks with a total of 12 megawatt-hour batteries, 20 commercial shophouses with about one megawatt-hour and five light industrial buildings with another one megawatt-hour.

sections.label: National distributed BESS capacity
sections.summary: About 10,000 HDB blocks hold 1.5 gigawatt-hours of BESS, plus two gigawatt-hours commercial and industrial, totalling 3.5 gigawatt-hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If I were to summarise a national technical summary, that is approximately 10,000 HDB blocks with a total distributed BESS capacity of 1.5 gigawatt-hours and additional commercial and industrial BESS of about two gigawatt-hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The national distributed storage is 3.5 gigawatt-hours, the equivalent to the output of a 500 megawatt gas plant running for seven hours.

sections.label: Solar plus BESS backup cost
sections.summary: Solar plus BESS, amortised over 15 years, costs $0.15 to $0.25 per kilowatt-hour for back-up power.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Solar plus BESS, amortised over 15 years, costs $0.15 to $0.25 per kilowatt-hour for back-up power.

sections.label: Constituency-scale microgrid task force proposal
sections.summary: A speaker urges the Ministry to approve a multi-agency task force to pilot the first constituency-scale microgrid with solar and BESS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And it can be built block by block, constituency by constituency, without waiting for a crisis to force our hand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to review and approve the establishment of a multi-agency task force, including the Energy Market Authority (EMA), HDB, the Building and Construction Authority and industry experts, to pilot the first constituency-scale microgrid with solar and BESS.

sections.label: Singapore power interruption statistics 2025
sections.summary: In 2025, average power interruption time was under one minute per customer on mainland Singapore, with about 0.02 interruptions per customer.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In 2025, the average power interruption time was less than one minute per customer on mainland Singapore and the average frequency of interruptions was about 0.02 times per customer.

sections.label: Future Grid Capabilities Roadmap and laboratory
sections.summary: EMA and SP Group developed the Future Grid Capabilities Roadmap, with the upcoming SP Technology Laboratory as one outcome.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: EMA and SP Group developed the Future Grid Capabilities Roadmap last year to chart a clear direction for building new capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: One concrete outcome is the upcoming SP Technology Laboratory, which will focus on developing new tools and solutions for grid planning and operations.

sections.label: Demand-side Flexibility Roadmap
sections.summary: EMA's Demand-side Flexibility Roadmap sets out how demand-side flexibility will work in practice.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: EMA's Demand-side Flexibility Roadmap sets out how this will work in practice.

sections.label: Virtual Power Plant pilot
sections.summary: EMA will also launch a Virtual Power Plant pilot.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: EMA will also launch a Virtual Power Plant pilot.

sections.label: Pulau Ubin Micro-Grid reliability upgrade
sections.summary: The 2013 Pulau Ubin Micro-Grid, solar PV with battery and diesel, serves about 30 consumers and its operator is upgrading it after reliability issues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The Pulau Ubin Micro-Grid was launched in 2013 as an R&D testbed to reduce reliance on diesel for power generation on the island.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: It is powered by solar PV, supported by a battery energy storage system and diesel generators, and serves about 30 residential and business consumers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Some system reliability issues have surfaced in recent years, and the micro-grid operator, EDP Renewables, is working to upgrade the system to enhance its overall reliability.

sections.label: Decarbonisation Grand Challenge funding
sections.summary: EMA will publish grant call results; the Government set aside $800 million under the Decarbonisation Grand Challenge for low-carbon technology research and innovation, including energy storage and grid modernisation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: EMA will publish the results of the grant call soon.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: This year, the Government has set aside $800 million under the Decarbonisation Grand Challenge, to support research and innovation in low-carbon technologies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: This includes energy storage systems and grid modernisation.

sections.label: Data centres and grid options
sections.summary: Data centres are energy guzzlers using diesel back-up; electricity imports, batteries, solar and micro-grids are options to consider for the grid of the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman
sentences.text: One is that, yes, we go into data centres, it is a highly huge power guzzler, typically about 70 MW to 100 MW per centre, and they are running on diesel as a back-up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman
sentences.text: So, this is something we may look into closely because that would create another set of carbon emission.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: I want to thank Mr Azhar Othman on his comments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: I fully agree that data centres, they are energy guzzlers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Electricity imports, hopefully, if we can get that coming, using renewable energy sources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Of course, batteries, solar, these will also be options that data centres can consider.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: And micro-grids, as the Member said, are additional augmentations to complement our existing grid and we certainly would want to keep this in view as we develop our grid of the future.
